# Harnessmith

> Harnessmith installs a portable personal coding-agent harness for Codex, Cursor, and Claude Code.
> This file is an operational guide for an LLM helping a user install or initialize it.

Project: https://www.npmjs.com/package/harnessmith
Release channel: npm registry (`latest` dist-tag)
Runtime: Node.js 24.12 or newer
Repository package manager: pnpm 10.13.0 (locked by `packageManager` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`)
Distribution command: npm / npx
Installed Harness runtime dependencies: none (the npm initializer dependencies are bundled; the
embedded Harness bundle is self-contained)

For a verified source checkout, install and build locally before invoking the CLI:

```bash
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
pnpm run build
node bin/harnessmith.mjs --help
```

For a source checkout, use `node bin/harnessmith.mjs` after the local build above. For normal installation,
use the published `npx --yes harnessmith` commands below.

Generic Harness environment overrides:

- `HARNESS_HOME`: resolved by the selected installation adapter.
- `HARNESS_MEMORY_HOME`: shared memory root, default `~/.agent-docs`.
- `HARNESS_PERSONAL_HOME`: user-owned personal rules and repository map, default `~/.agent-harness`.
- `HARNESS_REPOSITORY_ROOT`: repository collection root, default `~/git-repo`.
- `HARNESS_OWNER`: owner written into memory metadata.

Host-specific paths belong only to installation adapters. They must not be copied into the distributed Harness
template, its runtime field names, or its progressive documentation.

## Supported agents and destinations

- `codex`
  - Instructions: `$CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md`, default `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`
  - Harness: `$CODEX_HOME/agent-harness`
- `claude`
  - Active instructions: `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CLAUDE.md`, default `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`
  - Canonical copy: `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/AGENTS.md`
  - Harness: `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/agent-harness`
- `cursor`
  - Active project rule: `<project>/.cursor/rules/agent-harness.mdc`
  - Canonical copy: `<project>/.cursor/AGENTS.md`
  - Harness: `<project>/.cursor/agent-harness`
  - Cursor installation is project-scoped. Resolve `--project` to the intended repository; Harnessmith
    automatically uses its Git root when possible.

## LLM installation protocol

1. Verify the runtime with `node --version`. Stop and explain the requirement if Node.js is older than 24.12.
2. Determine the exact agent selection from the user's request. Accepted values are `codex`, `cursor`,
   `claude`, `claude-code`, and `all`. Never infer `all` from an ambiguous request.
3. If Cursor is selected, determine the intended project path. Ask the user if more than one repository is
   plausible. Prefer an absolute path.
4. Preview resolved destinations before writing:

   ```bash
   npx --yes harnessmith --agent <agents> --project <project-path> --dry-run --json
   ```

   Omit `--project` when Cursor is not selected. Read every JSON line, check that each destination is inside
   the selected Agent home or Cursor project, and inspect every output action:
   - `create`: no existing destination.
   - `replace-managed`: checksum matches the current installation record.
   - `conflict`: existing content is unmanaged or was modified after installation.
   Inspect each plan's `capabilities`: instruction following is advisory and permissions remain host-owned.
5. If the user explicitly requested installation and the preview matches the requested scope, install:

   ```bash
   npx --yes harnessmith --agent <agents> --project <project-path>
   ```

   Do not use `sudo`, do not delete existing files, and do not move unrelated files. A `conflict` is a
   blocker unless the user explicitly reviewed it and authorized `--force`; `--force` backs up the current
   destination before taking ownership. If the environment requires filesystem or network approval, request
   the minimum required permission.
6. Report every installed instruction path, Harness path, and backup path printed by the command.

## Initialization after installation

Harnessmith always initializes the user-owned personal overlay after a successful install and initializes
shared global memory unless `--no-init-global` was explicitly supplied. Existing personal files are never
overwritten. Verify them with:

```bash
node <harness-path>/bin/harness.mjs memory check global
node <harness-path>/bin/harness.mjs doctor
```

If the user intentionally installed with `--no-init-global` and later requests initialization, run:

```bash
node <harness-path>/bin/harness.mjs init global
```

The personal overlay can also be initialized independently and safely:

```bash
node <harness-path>/bin/harness.mjs init personal
```

Initialize project memory only when the task needs cross-session handoff, important user input, evidence,
unfinished work, or expensive discoveries:

```bash
node <harness-path>/bin/harness.mjs init project <absolute-project-path>
node <harness-path>/bin/harness.mjs memory check <absolute-project-path>
node <harness-path>/bin/harness.mjs validate --project <absolute-project-path>
```

If project-memory need is uncertain, ask the user. Do not initialize `.agent-docs` merely because the command
exists. Initialization adds `/.agent-docs/` to both the project-root `.gitignore` and `.ignore`.

## Backup and transaction guarantees

- Lexical and canonical containment is checked for outputs, backups, records, and ignore files. Existing
  symlink, junction, or reparse segments below an authorized root are rejected; do not bypass this check by
  moving files manually.
- Mutating lifecycle commands and status use a cross-process lock per Adapter. A lock failure means another
  operation may be active; report it and retry later instead of deleting the lock directory.
- Unmanaged or modified files are rejected by default and require explicit `--force` authorization.
- Existing instruction files are renamed in place to `<filename>.backup-<timestamp>`.
- Existing `agent-harness/` is renamed to `agent-harness.backup-<timestamp>`.
- Existing Harness `state/` is copied into the new installation and excluded from managed-runtime checksums.
- The personal overlay is user-owned; upgrade, restore, and uninstall do not remove or overwrite it.
- Install stages and JavaScript syntax-checks all selected rendered targets before replacement. Restore and
  uninstall instead preflight the exact recorded paths and backup relationships.
- If a selected target fails, Harnessmith rolls back destinations changed by that run.
- Each Adapter stores an installation record with checksums and backup relationships.
- `status` reports managed, modified, and missing outputs.
- `restore` restores one installation layer; `uninstall` restores every recorded layer to the pre-install
  state. Multi-Agent lifecycle actions preflight all targets and roll back the whole operation on failure.
  Both preserve `.agent-docs` memory and the personal overlay.
- Managed Cursor files are added to the repository-local Git exclude file and `.cursor/.ignore`; do not
  ignore or overwrite unrelated team rules in `.cursor/`.
- Never remove backup files unless the user explicitly asks after verifying the new installation.

## Non-interactive examples

The following examples use the published npm package. In a source checkout, replace `npx --yes harnessmith`
with `node bin/harnessmith.mjs` after completing the local build above.

```bash
# Codex global setup
npx --yes harnessmith --agent codex

# Claude Code global setup
npx --yes harnessmith --agent claude

# Cursor setup for one repository
npx --yes harnessmith --agent cursor --project /absolute/path/to/repository

# Install all supported agents; Cursor uses the specified repository
npx --yes harnessmith --agent all --project /absolute/path/to/repository

# Inspect ownership and file integrity
npx --yes harnessmith status --agent all --project /absolute/path/to/repository --json

# Recover one layer or fully uninstall
npx --yes harnessmith restore --agent codex
npx --yes harnessmith uninstall --agent codex
```

## Failure handling

- With `--json`, failures are one stderr JSON object. Exit 2 is a CLI usage error, 3 is a safety or integrity
  refusal, 4 is operation-lock contention, 5 is missing actionable installation state, and 1 is an
  unclassified internal failure. Preserve both code and message.
- A failed dry-run or an unexpected destination is a blocker; do not continue with installation.
- A `conflict`, `modified`, or missing backup is a blocker. Never add `--force` merely to make the command
  pass; obtain explicit user authorization after explaining what will be replaced.
- Preserve command stderr and report the failed phase without claiming success.
- Do not repair Node/npm/pnpm with `sudo`, change package-manager ownership, publish the package, configure a remote, or create
  a Git commit unless the user separately authorizes that action.
- Upgrade Cursor or Claude Code installations by rerunning `npx harnessmith`; do not invoke their embedded
  `harness install` command.

## Success criteria

- The requested Agent instruction files exist at the resolved destinations.
- `<agent-home>/agent-harness/manifest.json` exists.
- `<agent-home>/.harnessmith/install.json` exists and `status` reports every output as `managed`.
- `node <harness-path>/bin/harness.mjs --version` exits successfully.
- If initialization was requested, global memory check and `doctor` pass.
- If project memory was initialized, both ignore files contain `/.agent-docs/` and project validation passes.
